variants.cost: Per nonzero update: one selected-subgradient evaluation, one objective-value evaluation, one tangent norm, tangent scalar arithmetic, and one exponential-map evaluation. A combined value/subgradient Oracle can supply both quantities in one call; separate interfaces require separate calls. Curvature information, f* and a distance estimate are supplied inputs whose acquisition is not charged by the iteration count and is not claimed free. No exponential-map implementation cost or general runtime bound is provided by the source.
variants.name: Algorithm 1 with Strategy 2
variants.output: The generated iterates; pk upon the published zero-subgradient stopping test. No averaging or random output selection is specified.
public_inputs: Riemannian manifold, metric and exponential-map implementation
f and exact f*; exact value and selectable subgradient access
p0 in int dom f, a valid curvature lower bound kappa<0, and d0 or an estimate dhat>d0 for tuning
variants.query_and_update: At pk obtain sk in partial f(pk). If sk=0, stop at pk. Otherwise evaluate f(pk), set tk=alpha*(f(pk)-f*)/||sk||, and compute p(k+1)=Exp_pk(-tk*sk/||sk||). Increment k and repeat. The two occurrences of ||sk|| are intentional: tk is travel length, not the coefficient of sk in the exponential-map argument.
variants.requirements: Use the proper lower-semicontinuous convex function and complete Riemannian geometry defined in the Source. Each requested value must be finite and a subgradient must be available. The paper assumes the resulting sequence is well-defined and infinite for its analysis; domain invariance is not supplied by this record.
variants.state_and_initialization: Set p=p0 and k=0. Assume Omega*=argmin f is nonempty and d0=dist(p0,Omega*)>0. State consists of pk and k, together with fixed alpha and f*.
variants.tuning_and_stopping: Choose fixed 0<alpha<2*tanh(a*d0)/(a*d0), a=sqrt(abs(kappa)). Remark 1 permits replacing d0 by a supplied dhat>d0 in this bound. The published stopping test is a zero selected subgradient. No epsilon stopping rule or finite-horizon selector is prescribed. If f(pk)=f* while a nonzero subgradient is selected, Eq.(5) gives tk=0; such a step is outside the stated positive-step infinite-sequence regime, and no extra stopping rule is silently added here.
